body: The Slovenian landscape is generally very hilly and forested, with occasional agriculture.
A very significant portion of the coverage in Slovenia was taken on small roads deep inside forests.
Slovenian architecture is inspired by alpine styles, with light coloured walls, dark wooden details and semi-steep roofs. The most common roof shape is half-hipped.
The Slovene language is a Slavic language featuring the special letters Č, Š, and Ž. It is closely related to Croatian, Serbian and Montenegrin.
Slovenian bollards are white with a black top. The front reflector is typically bright red, while the back reflector is white.
Slovenian directional signs are yellow with a black border.
Slovenian kilometre markers have a distinct design with the road number in a yellow rectangle at the top left and a horizontal black line dividing the top and bottom.
Slovenian chevrons usually have red arrows on a white background, with a less common version having a black arrow on a white background.
Slovenian pedestrian signs have five stripes and a simply drawn person without a belt.
Slovenian roads commonly feature long outer dashes.
Slovenian street signs are commonly white with a metal border or red and attached to house walls. Most street names contain the word 'ulica'.
Slovenian house numbers are typically red with white text.
Slovenia uses a regular A-type guardrail with rounded edges, unlike Croatia which uses B-type guardrails with square edges.
A kozolec, a type of shed made of thin wooden beams with noticeable gaps, is very typical for Slovenia.
The tallest mountains in Slovenia are in the northwestern alpine region.
The east of the country has flat or rolling agricultural fields with no mountains or tall hills in view.
The coastal landscape is similar to the rest of the Adriatic coast, with white cliffs, bushy vegetation, vineyards, and Mediterranean architecture.
A wide valley going east to west, with mountains to the north and south, can be found in the southeast.
Italian bilingual signs can be found in the westernmost region.
Instead of the normal red house numbers, Ljubljana typically features green house numbers and occasionally green street signs.
Street signs in Celje feature the city's emblem: a blue shield with three yellow stars.
Street signs in Trbovlje feature the city’s coat of arms, which is a blue and green shield with a black crest.
